thread:
elaine_support: FYI customer 3927 reporting a sudden spike of 429s + large tail latency on their Dedicated pool, started ~09:12 UTC. ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/3927 :grimace:

michael_sre: Pulling metrics now — I'm seeing a sharp rise in 429s at 09:12 and CPU on the pool is only ~35%. interesting.

sophia_eng: Can you paste the quota config for that tenant? suspecting an asymmetric rate/unit misconfig during the quota migration we ran last night.

ryan_support: Posted customer repro payload in the ticket, they say requests are all small (short prompts) so token cost is low. they hit 429s immediately when burst starts.

michael_sre: Ran the admin check: `GET /admin/tenants/3927/limits` returns: ```{
  "rate_limit": 100,
  "rate_window": "minute",
  "concurrency": 8
}``` So their rate_limit is 100 per minute. autoscaler expects checks in req/sec equivalence. This looks like a minute/second mismatch leading to an effective 1.6 r/s cap.

elaine_support: So that would make bursty traffic exceed it quickly and trigger 429s even though GPUs aren't saturated?

michael_sre: Exactly. The rate-limiter is global per-tenant before routing to the pool. When it rejects requests the autoscaler never sees the queued load (we only scale on accepted queue length/behind-backpressure), so it didn't spin up more nodes. That's why pool CPU is low but clients see 429/latency.

jen_prod: Oof. Was this from the migration script? I thought we had conversion code.

ryan_support: Customer says they were on Dedicated before migration and we applied the new quota format last night.

autoscale-bot: [alert] quota-migration: tenant 3927 converted rate_window from "second" to "minute" at 2026-03-17T02:04:12Z by migration-service

sophia_eng: Repro steps I ran locally: send 300 short reqs in 30s -> immediate 429s. With a corrected rate_window to "second" (rate_limit 2 r/s ≈ 120/min) the same burst flows through and autoscaler reacts by +1 node in ~45s.

michael_sre: Proposed mitigation: update tenant config to use `rate_window: "second"` and set `rate_limit: 2` (or bump to 5 to match customer's expected burst window). Also add temporary bypass for dedicated pools to count queued requests toward autoscale metrics.

elaine_support: I'll ask customer if they're OK with a temporary bump while we fix migration logic. Can ops apply the quick fix?

michael_sre: ops, run: ```PATCH /admin/tenants/3927/limits
Content-Type: application/json
{ "rate_limit": 5, "rate_window": "second" }``` then `POST /ops/flush-rate-cache/3927`

jen_prod: Will follow up on migration-service: adding a validation that rejects `rate_window` values of "minute" for dedicated tenants (only allow "second"/"burst" enums). Also adding a unit-test for conversion math.

ryan_support: Customer agreed to temporary bump. I'll apply after hours and confirm with them.

michael_sre: After we applied the patch in staging repro, 429s dropped and tail latency normalized. I'll schedule a runbook entry: "quota-migration sanity checks" and add metric: `rate_limit_unit_mismatch_count` alert.

elaine_support: Great. Please post the ops runbook link here once ready and I'll close the support ticket once customer confirms. :thumbsup:

sophia_eng: Notes for postmortem: - root cause: migration converted per-second semantics to per-minute for this tenant - secondary effect: autoscaler doesn't see rejected requests - fix: immediate config patch + migration validation + autoscale metric tweak

michael_sre: Thanks everyone, I'll update the incident tracker with timestamps and LESSONS_LEARNED.

elaine_support: Closing loop: customer confirmed no more 429s at 10:02 UTC. Thanks team. :tada:
